3.1.vi: Production → product · Investment → benefit · Research → knowledge.
3.1.en: Production → product · Investment → benefit · Research → knowledge.

3.1.q: Which is a defining feature of a project in the lecture?
o: A well-defined goal with limited time and budget
3.1.vi: Project: chuỗi task, mục tiêu rõ, giới hạn time và budget.
3.1.en: A project: tasks, a well-defined goal, limited time and budget.

3.1.q: Which is listed as a common reason why software projects fail?
3.1.vi: Lý do thất bại: requirement mơ hồ/đổi, ước lượng thấp, giao tiếp kém, thiếu risk mgmt, test kém, thiếu kỹ năng.
3.1.en: Failure reasons: unclear requirements, underestimates, poor communication, no risk management, weak testing, missing skills.

3.2.q: Which role is NOT listed as responsible for software project management?
3.2.vi: Trách nhiệm: Program manager, Project manager, Team lead, Test manager.
3.2.en: Responsible roles: Program manager, Project manager, Team lead, Test manager.

3.2.q: Which role focuses on scope, schedule, cost, risks, communication and stakeholders?
3.2.vi: PM: scope, schedule, cost, risks, stakeholders. EM: chất lượng kỹ thuật. Team Lead: điều phối hằng ngày.
3.2.en: PM: scope, schedule, cost, risks, stakeholders. EM: technical quality. Team Lead: daily coordination.

3.2.q: Scope, WBS, estimates, schedule and staffing plan are outputs of:
3.2.vi: Planning: what/who/when/how much → scope, WBS, estimates, schedule, staffing plan.
3.2.en: Planning: what/who/when/how much → scope, WBS, estimates, schedule, staffing plan.

3.2.q: "Are tasks being performed according to the plan?" is the main question of:
3.2.vi: Executing: task có đúng plan → weekly plan, task đã giao, deliverable trung gian.
3.2.en: Executing: are tasks on plan → weekly plan, assigned tasks, intermediate deliverables.

3.3.q: Agile projects plan continuously in which smaller horizons?
3.3.vi: Agile lập kế hoạch liên tục theo release, sprint, day.
3.3.en: Agile plans continuously per release, sprint and day.

3.3.q: Which is part of the Software Development Plan (SDP) activities?
3.3.vi: Hoạt động SDP: ước lượng, lên phase, chọn process, giao vai trò, đào tạo, xác định và đánh giá rủi ro.
3.3.en: SDP activities: estimate, plan phases, define process, assign roles, plan training, identify and assess risks.

3.3.q: Why does a clear scope matter?
o: It helps estimate effort, schedule tasks, assign work and control changes
It removes the need for testing
It guarantees no requirement will change
3.3.vi: Scope rõ giúp ước lượng, xếp lịch, giao việc, kiểm soát thay đổi.
3.3.en: A clear scope helps estimate, schedule, assign work and control changes.

3.3.q: A WBS organizes the project into:
3.3.vi: WBS: phase → deliverable → task; nền tảng cho lập lịch và nhận diện rủi ro.
3.3.en: WBS: phases → deliverables → tasks; foundation for scheduling and risk identification.

3.3.vi: WBS = Work Breakdown Structure: chia scope dự án thành các phần việc nhỏ, quản lý được.
3.3.en: WBS = Work Breakdown Structure: breaks the project scope into smaller, manageable work items.

3.3.q: The SDP, which contains the budget, schedule, staffing and risk management plans, stands for:
3.3.vi: SDP = Software Development Plan: gồm budget & schedule, staffing, training, risk management, testing, deployment…
3.3.en: SDP = Software Development Plan: budget & schedule, staffing, training, risk management, testing, deployment…

3.4.q: An estimate based on the manager's experience of past projects is:
3.4.vi: Experience-based: kinh nghiệm. Algorithmic: công thức theo size và đặc điểm process.
3.4.en: Experience-based: past experience. Algorithmic: a formula from size and process traits.

3.4.q: Which statement about LOC is correct?
3.4.vi: LOC: đếm dòng chạy được, bỏ comment/dòng trống, phụ thuộc ngôn ngữ. FP: độc lập ngôn ngữ.
3.4.en: LOC: executable lines, no comments/blanks, language-dependent. FP: language-independent.

3.4.q: Which formula estimates project duration in the lecture?
A task needs 24 person-hours. Two students each work 3 hours/day. About how long does it take?
3.4.vi: $24 \div (2 \times 3) \approx 4$ ngày, nhưng thêm người không giảm thời gian tuyến tính.
3.4.en: $24 \div (2 \times 3) \approx 4$ days, though adding people is not linear.

3.4.vi: Story points = effort + complexity + uncertainty, ước lượng bằng Planning Poker (Fibonacci).
3.4.en: Story points = effort + complexity + uncertainty, estimated with Planning Poker (Fibonacci).

3.4.q: In size estimation, LOC and FP stand for:
3.4.vi: LOC = Lines of Code (phụ thuộc ngôn ngữ) · FP = Function Points (đo chức năng từ góc nhìn người dùng, độc lập ngôn ngữ).
3.4.en: LOC = Lines of Code (language-dependent) · FP = Function Points (functionality from the user's view, language-independent).

3.4.q: In the COCOMO formula $\text{Effort} = a \times (\text{KLOC})^{b}$, KLOC means:
3.4.vi: KLOC = kilo (nghìn) lines of code: kích thước phần mềm tính bằng nghìn dòng code (LOC ở 03#21; chữ K = kilo là quy ước đơn vị chung, slide không ghi).
3.4.en: KLOC = kilo (thousands of) lines of code: software size in thousands of LOC (LOC is on 03#21; K = kilo is the standard unit prefix, not spelled out on the slide).

3.5.q: The goal of project scheduling is to:
o: Assign the right people to the right tasks at the right time
Maximize the number of task dependencies
Add people whenever a project is late
Remove all slack time by adding staff
3.5.vi: Scheduling: đúng người, đúng việc, đúng lúc; giảm phụ thuộc, cân bằng tải.
3.5.en: Scheduling: right people, right tasks, right time; fewer dependencies, balanced load.

3.5.vi: Milestone: điểm kết thúc một giai đoạn. Deliverable: kết quả giao cho khách.
3.5.en: Milestone: end-point of a period. Deliverable: result delivered to customers.

3.5.vi: $\text{Slack} = \text{latest start} - \text{earliest start}$; task găng có slack = 0.
3.5.en: $\text{Slack} = \text{latest start} - \text{earliest start}$; critical tasks have zero slack.

3.5.q: In the slide example (T1 3d → T2 2d / T3 2d → T4 5d → T5 3d → T6 1d), if T3 is delayed by 1 day, the project takes:
3.5.vi: T3 nằm trên một đường găng (14 ngày), trễ 1 ngày thì dự án thành 15 ngày.
3.5.en: T3 is on a critical path (14 days); a 1-day delay makes the project 15 days.

3.5.q: Which tool does the lecture suggest to show a schedule?
3.5.vi: Thể hiện lịch bằng Gantt chart; quản lý task trên board (GitHub Projects, Jira, Trello).
3.5.en: Show the schedule as a Gantt chart; manage tasks on a board.

3.5.vi: CPM = Critical Path Method: tìm chuỗi task dài nhất, các task trên đó có slack = 0.
3.5.en: CPM = Critical Path Method: find the longest chain of tasks; tasks on it have zero slack.

3.6.q: Which is listed as an effect of risks on a project?
3.6.vi: Rủi ro ảnh hưởng: lịch/tài nguyên, chất lượng/hiệu năng, chi phí…

3.6.q: In the software risks table, "Staff turnover" affects the:
3.6.vi: Staff turnover, Management change, Hardware unavailability → Project.
3.6.en: Staff turnover, Management change, Hardware unavailability → Project.

3.6.vi: Requirements change, Specification delays, Size underestimate → Project và Product.
3.6.en: Requirements change, Specification delays, Size underestimate → Project and Product.

3.6.q: "Customers fail to understand the impact of requirements changes" is which risk type?
3.6.vi: Requirements risk: thay đổi cần thiết kế lại lớn; khách không hiểu tác động thay đổi.
3.6.en: Requirements risk: changes needing major rework; customers not understanding change impact.

3.6.q: "The organization is restructured so that different management are responsible for the project" is which risk type?
3.6.vi: Organizational: tái cấu trúc, khó khăn tài chính.

3.6.q: In risk analysis, loss can be expressed as:
o: Categorical (negligible … catastrophic) or a number representing cost
Only the number of affected users
3.6.vi: Loss: categorical hoặc một con số chi phí. Probability: categorical hoặc 0–100%.
3.6.en: Loss: categorical or a cost number. Probability: categorical or 0–100%.

3.6.q: Using the lecture's scale, what is the RE of a Likely × Serious risk?
3.6.vi: $75 \times 75 = 5{,}625$ (ví dụ: tổ chức tái cấu trúc).

3.6.q: Using the lecture's scale, what is the RE of a Seldom × Catastrophic risk?
3.6.vi: $25 \times 90 = 2{,}250$ (ví dụ: khó khăn tài chính, cắt ngân sách).

3.6.q: In risk analysis, RE stands for:
3.6.vi: Ở bài 03, RE = Risk exposure = Probability × Loss. Cẩn thận: ở bài 04, "RE" thường chỉ Requirements engineering.
3.6.en: In lecture 03, RE = Risk exposure = Probability × Loss. Careful: in lecture 04 "RE" usually means requirements engineering.

3.7.q: Which is NOT one of the risk planning strategies listed in the lecture?
3.7.vi: Slide liệt kê: avoidance, minimization, contingency plans, risk transfer, buying information.
3.7.en: The slide lists: avoidance, minimization, contingency plans, risk transfer, buying information.

3.7.q: The lecture's strategy for staff illness is to:
o: Reorganize the team so there is more overlap of work
3.7.vi: Staff illness: tổ chức lại team để công việc chồng lấn, hiểu việc của nhau.
3.7.en: Staff illness: reorganize the team for overlapping work.

3.7.q: For requirements changes, the lecture suggests:
o: Derive traceability information and maximize information hiding
Prepare a briefing for senior management
3.7.vi: Requirements changes: traceability để đánh giá tác động; tối đa information hiding.
3.7.en: Requirements changes: traceability to assess impact; maximize information hiding.

3.7.q: "Many requirements change requests and customer complaints" are indicators of which risk type?
3.7.vi: Dấu hiệu Requirements: nhiều change request, khách phàn nàn.
3.7.en: Requirements indicators: many change requests, customer complaints.

3.7.q: How should high-priority risks be handled during monitoring?
o: Reviewed at management progress meetings and reported weekly
Reviewed only at the end of the project
3.7.vi: Rủi ro ưu tiên cao: bàn ở họp tiến độ của ban quản lý, báo cáo hằng tuần.
3.7.en: High-priority risks: discussed at management progress meetings, reported weekly.
